What SharePoint allows, and what it does not

Everything in this document is built from out-of-the-box web parts and section settings. No custom code, no SPFx. Turn on "Show web parts" in the top bar to see which native part and which section setting produces each block on every page.

Fonts
SharePoint renders in Segoe UI. The Madsen design system asks for Ubuntu, Gotham and Lato, and none of them can be loaded on a modern page without SPFx or a custom font package uploaded by the tenant admin. This document is drawn in Segoe UI, which is what the dealer will actually see.
Colour
The theme gives us themePrimary plus a neutral ramp. themePrimary colours links, buttons, icons and the "Strong" section background, all at once. It is set to Power Systems blue #017FB0, the working tone from the Madsen palette, not the identity #00A4E3. The identity blue measures 2.83:1 against white text and fails even for large type. #017FB0 measures 4.50:1, exactly the AA threshold, which is why nothing sitting on the blue band is allowed a reduced opacity: any transparency drops it below.
Section backgrounds
Four options only: None (white), Neutral (light grey), Soft and Strong (themePrimary). Arbitrary background colours are not available, so every band in this document is one of those four.
Column widths
One, two, three columns, or a one-third sidebar left or right. The page header uses one-third text plus two-thirds photograph, which is a real SharePoint layout. 42/58 is not.
Images
The Image web part does not crop, it fits by row height. Mixed ratios are what produce today's ragged home grid. All eleven ship at 3:2, 1800 x 1200, and the tops at 12:5, 2880 x 1200.
Icons
The Quick links web part carries one icon per item, chosen from the Fluent library, or a custom image uploaded to Site Assets. Icons take themePrimary. That is how every tile grid in this document is built, and it is why the tiles carry an icon instead of the coloured left edge the earlier version used, which needs CSS and is not available.
Full width
Full-width sections exist on communication sites but accept only the Image and Hero web parts. A header with separate eyebrow, title and subtitle cannot be full width. It sits inside the 1236px canvas, with the section colour bleeding to the browser edge behind it.
Logos
SharePoint's own header carries one site logo and the site name, and renders it on every page for free. Madsen goes there. Madsen asked for FPT in the first fold, and the header takes only one logo, so FPT sits in a strip directly below it, on white, at 52px. That is the arrangement the brand standards ask for: the supplier logo present, but under the Madsen logo and smaller, never level with it. It costs one section on each of the twelve pages, and it leaves the footer at the same time. Showing FPT in both places is the duplication we removed for Madsen.
Text in images
Never. Not a SharePoint limit, a Madsen rule: the title comes from the web part so it stays translatable and readable by a screen reader. The Image web part's own text overlay is real text and is allowed, and that is what the home cards use.

Is all of this editable, one line at a time

Every device used in these layouts, and whether a Madsen editor can produce it from the page editor without any development. Three rows need confirmation inside the tenant, because they depend on settings an administrator controls rather than on the page editor.

The three rows marked Confirm: font colour in the Text web part toolbar, because the palette offered varies by tenant version, and the fallback is to leave headings dark and let the blue carry through icons, rules and links, which needs no per-character formatting. The People web part, because it reads the directory, so the eight Madsen contacts need job titles filled in on their Microsoft 365 profiles; if they are not, the same cards can be built as a Quick links grid with a photo per item. And the custom font package, which only a SharePoint administrator can answer.

Navigation

Eleven destinations plus News. Flat, they wrap onto two lines at the standard canvas and tell the dealer nothing about what belongs with what. Grouped under three headers they fit on one line, and the group name does the orienting. Communication sites support a cascading menu natively, so the grouping costs nothing but a decision. No page is renamed, moved or re-addressed.

A · Flat, all elevenReconstructed from the eleven destinations, not extracted from the live site.

Eleven items wrap. Full Dealers ends up next to Forms & Templates with nothing in common.

B · Grouped, three headersProposal. One menu is drawn open so the grouping reads without hovering.

Site settings → Navigation → add three parent links with no target page, then drag each destination under one of them. This is the one structural decision in this document: the July plan parked the regrouping as a future possibility, and putting the navigation on screen forces it now. The clickable prototype uses this menu, and it works. News sits beside Home as a top level entry, with no dropdown, because it is one destination and not a group.

Home

The approved card model: square card, title at the top, one line at the bottom, both over the photograph, the whole card clickable. Twelve cards now: the eleven destinations plus News, which Madsen asked for as a page of its own. The images were built with the upper and lower quarters kept clear so text never lands on a face.

Built as an Image web part per card in a three-column section, five sections deep, with the title as the image's own text overlay. That is how the eleven cards are on the page today, and it works. What has to change is the source files: all eleven at the same 3:2, and the duplicated text link under each card removed, since the whole card is already the link. The News band at the foot of the page is new: a News web part on a Neutral section, which lists the posts published on this site, newest first.

The page system

One skeleton for all twelve destinations, five sections deep. What changes between pages is the body, never the frame.

0 · Site chrome
SharePoint's own header and footer, set once in site settings and rendered on every page: Madsen logo and site name at the top, links at the bottom. Costs no section on any page.
1 · FPT strip
One-column section, no background. Text web part and Image web part, FPT at 52px. Requested by Madsen so the FPT relationship is visible in the first fold. Repeated on all twelve pages, since SharePoint has no global page banner. The Madsen logo in the site header went up with it, to 46px on the Extended header layout, so the supplier logo does not end up larger than the house it sits under.
2 · Page header
Two-column section, one-third left, Strong background. Text web part on the left with eyebrow, H1 and one subtitle line. Image web part on the right, 12:5 at 2880 x 1200. Kept short so the content starts high on the page.
3 · Body
Eight blocks, recombined per page: Text, Quick links with icons, numbered list, a full-width photographic band, Neutral-background callout, table, People and Document library. Text column never exceeds 70 characters.
4 · Closing band
One-column section, Neutral background, Text web part plus Button web part. Grey rather than blue, so the page has one large blue area and not three.
5 · Footer
SharePoint's own site footer, enabled in site settings. Same on every page, edited in one place.

Alternative header · Hero web part, one tile, full widthShown once for comparison. Full bleed, but eyebrow, title and subtitle collapse into Hero's own fields.

The Hero version bleeds edge to edge and reads stronger, and it removes the blue band from the header. It costs control: the scrim is SharePoint's, not ours, and the eyebrow has to live inside the title or disappear. The one-third split shown on every page below keeps all three text levels and is closer to what was already approved.

Communitas for Madsen

What this is

Layouts for the twelve pages of the Dealers Portal, drawn inside what SharePoint can actually build: out-of-the-box web parts and section settings only, no custom code.

Three things to know before you read it

  • It is drawn in Segoe UI, because that is what SharePoint renders. Ubuntu and Gotham, which the Madsen design system asks for, cannot be loaded on a modern page without custom development.
  • Power Systems blue carries the interface: section headings, icons, links, buttons and the header band. It is the working tone #017FB0, not the identity #00A4E3, which fails contrast against white text.
  • Turn on "Show web parts" to see the native part behind every block, and open the clickable prototype to walk the portal as a dealer would.

What the state marks mean

Real is Madsen copy already in production, only reorganised here. Mixed is a real page still carrying Microsoft template residue. Proposal means the live page has no Madsen copy at all and everything shown is our suggestion.

Five of the twelve pages are running Microsoft template text in production right now: Full Dealers, Training, Sales & Marketing Materials, Forms & Templates and Products Documentation. That copy can be deleted today, before any of this is built.

One correction to the July plan

the test page was going to be unpublished. It should not be. It holds the only end to end warranty claim procedure on the portal, and Warranty & Claims links to it. Rename it and publish it properly instead.
